newsitem.title: USA: Intl Paper sees improving fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Intl Paper sees improving fundamentals.

text.p: International Paper Co, reporting lower fourth-quarter net income, said fundamentals in its market are improving and that it expects pricing for its products to improve early this year.

The company reported per-share profit from continuing operations of $0.33, slightly above analysts' consensus estimate of $0.31 per share, before charges for the writedown of its investment in its Scitex operations.
But IP warned that although it expects pricing to improve, "the impact of current low prices are likely to continue to affect earnings in the short-term."
The company said its recent restructuring was not able to overcome the market conditions of 1996.

"Although our profit-improvement programs continue to be successful and we restructured businesses to enhance their profitability, we were not able to offset the poor market conditions that marked 1996, said International Paper's chairman and chief executive officer, John Dillon.
"While it was an extremely difficult year for the industry, our internal business improvements will yield sustained long-term benefits for International Paper," Dillon said.
"As we begin a new year, marketplace fundamentals are improving. Volumes are good, and inventories are declining," Dillon said.
